Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}xy\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path along the line segment from the point $(-1,-2)$ to the point $(2,4),$ as shown above?

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=⟨3t-1,\,6t-2⟩.$*
solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a line segment with endpoints $(-1,-2)$ and $(2,4).$ It can be parametrized as 

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(-1+t(2-(-1))),\,(-2+t(4-(-2)))⟩ \\  & =⟨3t-1,\,6t-2⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$

Computing $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6t-2)=6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(3t-1)\cdot (6t-2) \\  & =18{t}^{2}-12t+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}f(r(t))\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(18{t}^{2}-12t+2)\cdot 6\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =12{\int }_{0}^{1}(9{t}^{2}-6t+1)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
